source: library/zagier-the-dilogarithm-function/zagier-the-dilogarithm-function.pdf = Zagier, The Dilogarithm Function (2007), II.1 B

gates.claim: V_j == 3*Dtilde at some integer branch offset (n,m)
V - 3*Dtilde is branch noise (pi^2-rational real part), not transcendental
sum_j Re Dtilde is an exact rational multiple of pi^2/2
gates.note: The sum rule says sum_j Re V_j = -3 pi^2/2. If V = 3*Dtilde then sum_j Re Dtilde = -pi^2/2, i.e. ratio = -1.

gates.claim: the residual V - 3*Dtilde has an exact closed form: pi i (2b+k) u - b^2 pi^2
gates.exact_restatement: sum_j Re Dtilde(y_j) == pi^2/2 - (2/3) pi theta,  theta = arg y_1
gates.negative_result: The pi*theta term is NOT in pi^2 Q, so the sum rule does NOT reduce to the vanishing of a class in R/(pi^2/2)Z under this identification. SCOPE-(a): this set-up does not close. It does NOT exclude an enhanced-dilogarithm formulation at a different covering point or on a different Bloch element -- no invariant forbids that, so no scope-(b) claim is made.

verdict: REFUTED (scope-a): V is NOT 3*Dtilde at any integer branch offset; the residual is exactly pi i (2b+k) u - b^2 pi^2 (G4), leaving a pi*arg(y_1) term outside pi^2 Q. The sum rule does not reduce to a mod-pi^2/2 rationality statement under this identification.
scope: Numerical only. A positive result would REFRAME the open problem (transcendental evaluation -> rationality mod pi^2/2), not prove the sum rule. Scope-(a) throughout: nothing here excludes any ingredient.
